(iv) Cr3+ with excess NaOH precipitates Cr(OH)3 (Cr3+ d3, paramagnetic).

- Diamagnetic: substances with all electrons paired.
- Paramagnetic: have unpaired electrons.
(i) Cr2O3 (Cr3+) has 3 unpaired electrons → paramagnetic.
(ii) N2 (diatomic nitrogen) has a closed-shell configuration → diamagnetic.
(iii) ZnCl2 (Zn2+) has d10 configuration → diamagnetic.
(iv) Cr(OH)3 (Cr3+) has 3 unpaired electrons → paramagnetic.
Step 3: Count reactions where indicated product is diamagnetic.
Only reactions (ii) and (iii) produce diamagnetic products.
Thus total number = 2.

Step-by-step reasoning:

(i) Na₂Cr₂O₇ with KCl and fractional crystallisation typically yields K₂Cr₂O₇ (or KCr(SO₄)₂ etc.) containing Cr(VI). In K₂Cr₂O₇, Cr is in +6 oxidation state with d0 configuration → diamagnetic. However, fractional crystallisation of Na₂Cr₂O₇/KCl often isolates K₂Cr₂O₇ which is diamagnetic. But the problem likely expects the product containing Cr after fractional crystallisation to be Cr(III) or Cr(VI)? Need check: Na₂Cr₂O₇ + KCl, fractional crystallisation could produce K₂Cr₂O₇ (Cr VI) or KCrO₃? Usually Na₂Cr₂O₇ + KCl gives K₂Cr₂O₇ and NaCl; Cr remains as Cr(VI). Cr(VI) d0 → diamagnetic. However many exam questions treat Cr(III) as paramagnetic. But fractional crystallisation of Na₂Cr₂O₇ with KCl might produce K₂Cr₂O₇ (Cr VI) which is diamagnetic. However ambiguous.

(ii) Cr³⁺ with excess NaOH gives Cr(OH)₃ precipitate. Cr(III) d³ → paramagnetic (three unpaired electrons).

(iii) CoCl₂ with NH₄Cl, excess NH₃, air bubbled through, charcoal. Typical procedure to isolate Co(II) or Co(III)? Excess NH₃ complexes Co²⁺ to [Co(NH₃)₆]²⁺ which is usually low-spin d⁷ → one unpaired electron → paramagnetic. Charcoal may reduce? Air bubbled suggests oxidation maybe to Co³⁺? But likely product containing Co is [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₂ or Co(OH)₃? Co(III) low-spin d⁶ → diamagnetic? However Co(III) with NH₃ typically forms low-spin [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ which is diamagnetic (t2g⁶). But with excess NH₃ and air, could oxidize Co²⁺ to Co³⁺ giving diamagnetic complex. However typical exam: CoCl₂ + NH₃ gives [Co(NH₃)₆]²⁺ paramagnetic. Given air bubbled through, might oxidize to Co³⁺? Unclear. Assume product is Co(II) complex → paramagnetic.

(iv) (NH₄)₂Cr₂O₇ on heating decomposes to Cr₂O₃, N₂, H₂O. Cr₂O₃ contains Cr(III) d³ → paramagnetic.

Thus likely reactions (ii), (iii), (iv) give paramagnetic products; (i) gives diamagnetic. So total paramagnetic reactions = 3.

But need decide (i). Fractional crystallisation of Na₂Cr₂O₇ with KCl often yields K₂Cr₂O₇ (Cr VI) diamagnetic. So answer 3.

However many might think Cr(III) formed → paramagnetic. But fractional crystallisation of dichromate with chloride typically yields chromate? Actually Na₂Cr₂O₇ + KCl → K₂Cr₂O₇ + NaCl; Cr stays VI. So diamagnetic.

Thus answer 3.

But the problem asks total number of reactions in which the indicated product is paramagnetic. So count among (i)-(iv). Likely answer 3.

Thus answer integer 3.
